cases.description: Leading/trailing spaces are stripped and multiple interior spaces collapse to a single space
TRIM only removes the regular ASCII space character (decimal 32); it does NOT remove other whitespace such as a tab (CHAR(9)), so the leading tab survives untouched
cases.expected_note: Microsoft docs: "the TRIM function was designed to trim the 7-bit ASCII space character (value 32) from text" -- it does not generalize to other whitespace. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: TRIM does not remove the non-breaking space character (CHAR(160), HTML  ) even though it renders as whitespace -- a real, documented, and easy-to-miss cross-engine divergence point since data pasted from web pages is full of CHAR(160)
cases.expected_note: Microsoft docs state explicitly: "by itself, the TRIM function does not remove the nonbreaking space character (which has a decimal value of 160 and is commonly used in web pages as the HTML entity  )." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: A string with only single spaces between words passes through unchanged
Length probe for the leading-tab case: if TRIM leaves the tab in place the result is 6 (tab + 5 letters); an engine that also strips tabs returns 5
cases.expected_note: Microsoft docs: "the TRIM function was designed to trim the 7-bit ASCII space character (value 32) from text", so a tab (CHAR(9)) survives and LEN stays 6. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: Identity probe for the same case: CODE of the first surviving character is 9 (the tab) if TRIM left it alone, and 72 (the letter H) if the engine stripped it
cases.expected_note: Numeric companion to TRIM_tab_not_removed -- CODE() makes the difference comparable across engines without depending on how a reader renders a tab. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: Same probe for a leading line feed (CHAR(10)): 6 if the line feed survives TRIM, 5 if the engine strips it
cases.expected_note: CHAR(10) is not the ASCII space (32), so documented Excel TRIM leaves it untouched. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: The tab probe written with UNICHAR instead of CHAR, so the code point is unambiguous and does not depend on the engine's current code table
cases.expected_note: UNICHAR(9) is U+0009 on every engine; CHAR(9) depends on the active code table (LibreOffice help: CHAR "converts a number into a character according to the current code table"). Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: A genuine non-breaking space (U+00A0) on each side of the text: 7 if TRIM keeps both, 5 if an engine treats them as trimmable whitespace
cases.expected_note: Microsoft docs: "by itself, the TRIM function does not remove the nonbreaking space character (which has a decimal value of 160 ...)", so both non-breaking spaces survive and LEN stays 7. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: Identity probe for the same string: the first surviving character must still be the non-breaking space, code point 160
cases.expected_note: Written with UNICHAR rather than CHAR so the input is a real U+00A0 regardless of the engine's code table; pairs with TRIM_nonbreaking_space_not_removed, which uses CHAR(160). Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: A leading zero-width space (U+200B) -- invisible, but not the ASCII space -- so TRIM should leave it and LEN should stay 6
cases.expected_note: TRIM targets only the 7-bit ASCII space (32); U+200B is neither that nor a control character (so CLEAN does not remove it either). Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9

cases.description: Control case: ordinary spaces only. Leading and trailing runs are stripped and the interior run collapses to one space, leaving "a b" -- length 3
cases.expected_note: Baseline showing that the divergences in the other cases are about NON-space whitespace, not about TRIM's core space handling. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/trim-function-410388fa-c5df-49c6-b16c-9e5630b479f9
